correctness.rationale: For Cr_n (n≥3), exact zero constraints for A_i and B_i are q−1_{i∈Y}=1 and p−1_{i∈X}=1 when zero, respectively. For valid perfect-Roman assignments, totality iff at least 2 positive vertices on each bipartition side; then all positive vertices have positive cross-neighbors. Partition indices into X∩Y, X\Y, Y\X, remaining, giving multinomial signed-zero independent factors F_n. Enumerate all one-positive-side exceptions E_n, correct by inclusion-exclusion intersection n z^4; this gives boxed full polynomial. Classify weight 6: n≥4 has p=q=1 and count n(n−1)+n(n−1)^2=n²(n−1); n=3 additionally 13 giving 31. Independently enumerated every literal adjacency labeling for n=3..5, obtaining min6 counts31,48,100, and compared to exact polynomial.

originality.rationale: Almulhim (2023) introduced TPR, gives complete multipartite special cases (including K_n,n) but crowns K_n,n minus a matching are NOT complete multipartite for n≥3. Published Resultary crown perfect Roman minimum4 uses no positive-neighbor condition and does not imply total perfect full polynomial. Special n=3 is C6 and its minimum6 is already known; the full n-family and all coefficients are the new statement. Unindexed equivalent count remains bibliographic risk.
